title: Laptop cannot connect to Wi-Fi
description: Answer a few questions to find out whether the problem is your laptop, the router or your internet service.

nodes.text: Can other devices (such as a phone) connect to the same Wi-Fi and get online?
nodes.help: Use a phone on the same network. If you are not sure, choose No.

options.label: Yes, other devices work
No, they cannot get online either

nodes.text: Is Wi-Fi turned on in the laptop, with Airplane mode off?
nodes.help: Look at the Wi-Fi or Airplane icon near the clock, or in Settings.

options.label: Yes, Wi-Fi is on
No, it is off or Airplane mode is on

nodes.text: Does the laptop list any available wireless networks?

options.label: Yes, I can see networks
No, the list is empty

nodes.text: What happens when you try to join your network?

options.label: It fails, or asks for a password again
It says connected, but websites will not load

nodes.title: The problem is probably your router or internet service
nodes.summary: Because other devices are also offline, your laptop is likely fine. Check for an outage and restart the modem and router in the right order.
nodes.professionalHelp: If the router's internet light stays red after a restart, contact your internet provider.

nodes.title: Turn Wi-Fi on
nodes.summary: Switch off Airplane mode and enable Wi-Fi in Settings or with the Fn key shown on your keyboard. Then connect to your network.

nodes.title: Check the wireless adapter
nodes.summary: The laptop cannot see any networks, which points to a disabled adapter, a driver problem or a hardware switch.
nodes.professionalHelp: If no Wi-Fi adapter appears in Device Manager even after a restart and reinstall, the adapter may have failed and a technician should check it.

nodes.title: Re-enter the network details
nodes.summary: Forget the saved network and join again. Double-check the password for upper and lower-case letters.

nodes.title: Connected but no internet
nodes.summary: The laptop is joined to Wi-Fi but cannot reach the internet. Refresh the network configuration and try a different DNS server.

title: Laptop will not start
description: Work out whether the charger, battery, screen or software is stopping your laptop from starting.

nodes.text: When you press the power button, do any lights come on or do you hear the fan?

options.label: Yes, something lights up or spins
No, nothing at all

nodes.text: With the charger plugged into a socket you know works, does the charging light come on?
nodes.help: Check the light on the laptop or on the charger itself.

options.label: Yes, there is a charging light
No light at all

nodes.text: Is the screen completely black even though lights or fans are on?

options.label: Yes, black screen
No, I see a logo or something on screen

nodes.text: If you connect an external monitor, does it show a picture?
nodes.help: Press Windows+P or the display key after connecting it.

options.label: Yes, the monitor works
No, or I have no monitor to try

nodes.text: Does it get stuck on a logo or keep restarting?

options.label: Yes, it is stuck or restarting
No, it starts but shuts down shortly after

nodes.title: Let it charge, then reset the power
nodes.summary: A deeply drained battery can take 30 minutes before the laptop starts. After that, do the power reset from the guide.

nodes.title: Charger or power socket problem
nodes.summary: No charging light usually means a faulty charger, cable or socket. Test a different socket and a compatible charger.
nodes.professionalHelp: If a second charger and socket also give no light, the charging port or battery may need professional repair.

nodes.title: Internal display problem
nodes.summary: The laptop runs, but the built-in screen does not show it. You can keep working on an external monitor while you arrange repair.
nodes.professionalHelp: The screen, its cable or backlight likely need repair by a qualified technician.

nodes.title: Possible hardware fault
nodes.summary: Lights on with no picture can mean failed memory, motherboard or display. Try the power reset in the guide first.
nodes.professionalHelp: If the power reset does not help, have a qualified technician inspect it. Do not open the laptop yourself.

nodes.title: Startup or update problem
nodes.summary: Restart loops are often caused by failed updates or system file damage. Back up your files if you can and follow the guides.
nodes.professionalHelp: If it never reaches the desktop, ask a technician to recover your files before reinstalling Windows.

nodes.title: Probably overheating
nodes.summary: A laptop that shuts itself down soon after starting often protects itself from heat. Check the vents and surface.

title: Phone will not charge
description: Find out whether the cable, the port, the software or the battery is the problem.

nodes.text: Does the phone charge when you use a different cable and adapter?

options.label: Yes, it charges with another cable or adapter
No, it still does not charge

nodes.text: Can you see lint or dirt in the phone's charging port with a torch?

options.label: Yes, there is debris
No, the port looks clean

nodes.text: Is the phone swollen, unusually hot, or does it smell of burning or chemicals?
nodes.help: These can be signs of a damaged battery.

options.label: Yes, one of these
No, it looks normal

nodes.text: After a restart and 30 minutes on the charger, does the phone show any sign of life?

options.label: Yes, it wakes or shows a charging icon
No, still dead

nodes.title: Replace the faulty cable or adapter
nodes.summary: Your old cable or adapter has failed. Use a good-quality one from the phone maker or a certified brand.

nodes.title: Carefully clean the port
nodes.summary: Power the phone off and remove lint with a wooden or plastic pick. Avoid metal tools, liquids and compressed air.

nodes.title: Stop using the phone
nodes.summary: A swollen or very hot battery can be a fire risk. Switch the phone off, unplug it and keep it away from flammable items.
nodes.professionalHelp: Contact the manufacturer or an authorised service centre before using or charging it again.

nodes.title: Likely a software or deep-discharge issue
nodes.summary: Keep charging and update the phone. Then check what drains the battery.

nodes.title: The battery or charging port may need repair
nodes.summary: You have ruled out the cable, dirt and software basics.
nodes.professionalHelp: Take it to the manufacturer or an authorised repair shop. Do not open the phone.
